title: Pilgrim, Burdened with Thy Sin
description: Pilgrim, Burdened with Thy Sin in Tonic Solfa to HOLLINGSIDE, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 270 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Invitation”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens Double (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HOLLINGSIDE; any other Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Pil-grim, bur-dened with thy sin, Come the way to Zi-on's gate, There, till mer-cy speaks with-in, Knock, and weep, and watch and wait Knock he knows the sin-ner's cry, Weep he loves the mourn-er's tears, Watch for sa-ving grace is nigh, Wait till heav-enly grace ap-pears.

lines: Pilgrim, burdened with thy sin,
Come the way to Zion's gate,
There, till mercy speaks within,
Knock, and weep, and watch and wait —
Knock — he knows the sinner's cry,
Weep — he loves the mourner's tears,
Watch — for saving grace is nigh,
Wait — till heavenly grace appears.
Hark, it is thy Saviour's voice!
"Welcome, pilgrim, to thy rest."
Now within the gate rejoice,
Safe, and owned, and bought and blest —
Safe — from all the lures of vice,
Owned — by joys the contrite know,
Bought — by love and life the price,
Blest — the mighty debt to owe!
Holy pilgrim! what for thee,
In a world like this, remains?
From thy guarded breast shall flee
Fear, and shame, and doubt and pains —
Fear — the hope of heaven shall fly,
Shame — from glory's view retire,
Doubt — in full belief shall die,
Pain — in endless bliss expire.

licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to HOLLINGSIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
